_nota: Curiosidades del mapa mural, en inglés como todo el mural. Cada texto lleva sus fuentes (consultadas el 2026-10-22, con preferencia por DOC, Te Ara, NZHistory, GeoNet, NIWA y NZKGI). Donde las fuentes difieren, el texto usa la cifra o el rango que todas sostienen; el detalle está en 'nota'.

ave.texto: The bird. Five species, none of which can fly; they are mostly active at night. The only bird with nostrils at the tip of its beak: it sniffs out worms underground. Its egg weighs up to a fifth of the mother. About 70,000 are left, and unprotected populations shrink about 2% a year.
ave.nota: Población: DOC dice unos 70.000; Save the Kiwi, unos 68.000. Huevo: DOC, 15 a 20 % del peso de la hembra.
ave.credito: Drawings after J. G. Keulemans, North-Island kiwi, in W. L. Buller, A History of the Birds of New Zealand (1888), public domain; and a photo by André Karwath, CC BY-SA 2.5.

fruta.texto: The fruit. It began as the “Chinese gooseberry”: teacher Isabel Fraser brought the seeds from China in 1904, and the vines first fruited in Whanganui in 1910. In 1959 Turners and Growers renamed it “kiwifruit” to sell it in the United States. About 80% of the crop grows in Bay of Plenty, and Te Puke calls itself the kiwifruit capital of the world.
fruta.nota: Bay of Plenty: 79 % (NZKGI Kiwifruit Book 2024) a 81 % (informe previo a la cosecha 2024). «Capital mundial» es un apodo de Te Puke, no una medición.

gente.texto: The people. By 1917 New Zealand soldiers in the First World War were being called “Kiwis”; after the Second World War the name spread to all New Zealanders.
gente.nota: Se dejó afuera la betún Kiwi: Te Ara la menciona pero no dice que el apodo venga de ahí.

geografia.texto: The plate boundary runs about 600 km along the Southern Alps, which rise 10 mm or more a year. It last broke in 1717; there is a 75% chance of a big quake in the next 50 years.
geografia.nota: Largo: unos 600 km en tierra (GNS), 650 km (Te Ara), 800 km con el tramo submarino (AF8). La probabilidad es de un estudio de 2021.

geografia.texto: The lake fills a supervolcano. Its Ōruanui eruption, about 25,500 years ago, threw out over 1,000 km³ of material.
geografia.nota: Te Ara da unos 26.500 años. «La supererupción más reciente del mundo» no figura en GeoNet ni en Te Ara: no se usa.

geografia.texto: GeoNet locates about 20,000 a year (22,904 in 2024); only 100 to 250 are strong enough to be felt.
geografia.nota: Sentidos: GeoNet FAQ dice unos 250; una noticia de GeoNet, 100 a 150; Te Ara, 150 a 200.

geografia.texto: Milford Sound gets about 6,700 mm a year (9,259 mm in 2016), one of the wettest places in the country.
geografia.nota: Cifras de los informes climáticos de NIWA. No es el lugar más lluvioso: en la divisoria de los Alpes caen más de 10.000 mm (Te Ara).

slang: holiday house (crib in the far south)

historia.texto: Polynesian voyagers, the ancestors of Māori, settle the islands.
Dutch navigator Abel Tasman sights the coast; after a clash in Golden Bay he leaves without landing.
James Cook lands at Tūranganui-a-Kiwa (Gisborne) and goes on to map both islands.
The Treaty of Waitangi is first signed at Waitangi, Bay of Islands, on 6 February: now Waitangi Day.
The first self-governing country where all women can vote in national elections.
Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reach the top of Everest.
Te reo Māori becomes an official language.
The Christchurch earthquake of 22 February kills 185 people.

mapa.texto: New Zealand's largest known living kauri tree: about 51 m tall, 13.8 m around and some 1,500 years old.
The glowworms are larvae of a fungus gnat found only in New Zealand; they glow to lure insects into sticky threads.
The Shire set from The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit films, on a family farm. Tours run daily.
Home of the kea, the world's only alpine parrot, now nationally endangered. Clever and curious: never feed them.
The world's first commercial bungy jump (43 m), opened by AJ Hackett and Henry van Asch in 1988.
